div.div: One sentence here buys you the rest of the interview.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 366px; margin-left: 40px;

div.div: "I’ll design the feed read path and leave posting, moderation and notifications out — say if you’d rather I covered those instead."

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 770px; height: 1px; padding-top: 399px; margin-left: 25px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-muted); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-style: italic; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: That sentence is the cut line. Without it, every later stage is a guess about a product nobody agreed on.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 439px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Interviewers grade the split and the cut, not the length. Functional gets verbs, non-functional gets numbers, and out-of-scope gets said out loud rather than assumed.
